summary: Kenneth K. Tanaka is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at UC Berkeley under Padmanabh S. Jaini. He held posts at the Institute of Buddhist Studies, Musashino University, and served as President of the International Association of Shin Buddhist Studies.

Kenneth R. Valpey is a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and philosophy who studied at the University of California, Santa Barbara. He taught Ravi M. Gupta and held a post at The Chinese University of Hong Kong.

Kenryo Minowa is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo. He held faculty posts at Aichi Gakuin University, the University of Tokyo, and Rissho University, and headed the Japanese Association of Indian and Buddhist Studies.
Kenryu Nishio is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology who earned a doctorate in literature from Otani University. He has served as professor emeritus at Hanazono University.
Kenryu Tsuji was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University and the University of Toronto.

Kenryu Tsukinowa was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Bukkyo University. He was a professor at Koyasan University, Seizan College, and Shuchiin University, and professor emeritus at Ryukoku University.
Kenshi Kusano is a scholar in Buddhist studies, history/archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Otani University, where he also served as a professor around 2003.
Kenta Suzuki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University. He served as an associate professor at Hokkaido Musashi Women's Junior College around 2013.

Kenyu Mitomo is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned his MA and doctorate at Rissho University and studied at UC Berkeley. He served as Dean of Buddhist Studies at Rissho University from 1968 to 2015.

Kevin A. Vose is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He earned his BA at Bates College and his MA and PhD at the University of Virginia, studying under doctoral supervisor Jeffrey Hopkins and traditional teacher Khen Rinpoche Ngawang Jinpa.
Kevin Buckelew is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at Sarah Lawrence College. His doctoral supervisors included Chün-fang Yü, Bernard Faure, and Zhaohua Yang.
Kexin Zheng is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. She is a PhD candidate at Leiden University under the doctoral supervision of Peter C. Bisschop.

Khakyab Dorje was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and Khenchen Tashi Özer, among others. His students included Kalu Rinpoche.
Kham Sum Zilnön Gyepa Dorjé studied under Shenphen Nangwa and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He also taught Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.

Khammai Dhammasami is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his DPhil at the University of Oxford. He served as a fellow at the Oxford Centre for Buddhist Studies, professor at International Theravāda Buddhist Missionary University, and founded the Shan State Buddhist University.
Khangsar Tenpe Wangchuk was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under traditional teachers Jampal Gyepe Dorje and Lodro Gyatso.
Khen Gen Jampal Dorjé studied under Shenphen Nangwa and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.
Khenchen Ngawang Khyen Rab Gyatso studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Trulshik Rinpoche.

Khenchen Palden Sherab Rinpoche was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Gochen and Riwoche Monasteries and under Dudjom Rinpoche, later chairing the Nyingma section at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies from ~1967 to 1984.
Khenchen Tashi Özer studied under Patrul Rinpoche, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye. His students included Khakyab Dorje and Shechen Gyaltsab.
